Monitoring continuously observes production metrics, logs, and alerts to find anomalies and judge system health.·A login error rate can cross a threshold, trigger an alert, and connect its time window, request logs, and running version. This provides signals from real use after release. One test report only records some checks at one time and cannot replace production monitoring.

↳Monitoring continuously watches production signals; a screenshot or anecdote cannot replace the time series.

What decision monitoring enables

Choose signals that reflect user health: Login error rate, checkout success rate, request latency, and key logs show whether people are affected. Metrics need a time range and threshold, not a dashboard no one can judge.

An alert should return to runtime facts: When an anomaly appears, inspect the version, related requests, and scope, then decide to pause, disable a flag, roll back, or fix forward. Monitoring detects and supports judgment; it does not repair by itself.

What it is not

Monitoring is neither a one-time test report nor collecting many logs. It continuously produces actionable production signals and alerts; charts without thresholds, version association, or response actions rarely help stop impact quickly.
